resources.string: Start by connecting to a computer
For devices without root, you need to use adb to start Porter (requires computer connection). This process needs to be repeated every time the device is restarted. Please read the help.

%1$s

* There are some other considerations, please confirm that you have read the help first.

On Android 11 or above, you can enable Wireless debugging and start Porter directly from your device, without connecting to a computer.

Please view the step-by-step guide first.
Before Android 11, connecting to a computer is required to enable Wireless debugging.

Please enable \"Wireless debugging\" in \"Developer options\". \"Wireless debugging\" is automatically disabled when network changes.\n\nNote, do not disable \"Developer options\" or \"USB debugging\", or Porter will be stopped.
Please try to disable and enable \"Wireless debugging\" if it keeps searching.
Can\'t connect to wireless debugging service.\n\nPlease ensure that Porter is whitelisted in all firewall, ad-block, VPN, or similar apps that can restrict network access.
Wireless debugging is not enabled.\nNote, before Android 11, to enable wireless debugging, computer connection is a must.
USB debugging is not enabled.\nPlease enable it in \"Developer Options\".

On Android 14, installing/updating Porter with the Package Installer revokes the ^1 permission, which is required to enable the accessibility service for pairing.

To grant it, run the following ADB command:

^2

After running the command, you may continue with the pairing process.

Note: you can bypass this by installing/updating Porter with ADB.

Please enable the accessibility service to start the pairing process. This allows Porter to detect the pairing code.\n\nThe accessibility service will turn off after the pairing attempt, or if no code is found within one minute. Porter will show the result and let you retry.

Please start pairing by performing the following steps:
- Navigate to "Developer Options"
- Enable "USB debugging" and "Wireless debugging"
- Tap the left side of "Wireless debugging"
- Tap "Pair device with pairing code." Porter will automatically detect the pairing code.
The system requires the pairing dialog to always be visible. Using split-screen mode is the only way to let this app and the system dialog be visible at the same time.
Unable to generate key for wireless debugging.\nThis may be because the KeyStore mechanism of this device is broken.

Wireless debugging is on, but it does not recognize Porter. Porter has to be paired with wireless debugging on this device before it can start this way. That is needed once, and again whenever the pairing is lost, for example after Porter\'s app data is cleared or Porter is removed from the list of paired devices.\n\nChoose Pairing and follow the steps, then start Porter again.
A notification from Porter will help you complete the pairing.
Navigate to \"Developer Options\", then enable \"USB debugging\" and \"Wireless debugging\".
Tap the left side of \"Wireless debugging\", then tap \"Pair device with pairing code.\" Enter the code in the notification to complete pairing.
The pairing process needs you to interact with a notification from Porter. Please allow Porter to post notifications.
MIUI users may need to switch notification style to \"Android\" from \"Notification\" - \"Notification shade\" in system settings.
Otherwise, you may not able to enter the pairing code from the notification.
Go back to Porter and start Porter.
Porter needs to access the local network. It is controlled by the network permission.

Some systems (such as MIUI) disallow apps to access the network when they are not visible, even if the app uses a foreground service. Please disable battery optimization features for Porter on such systems.
If you use Magisk, %1$s is another option. Apps need explicit support for %2$s.
Apps that have requested or declared the Porter permission will show here.
You will need to reconfigure your intents with the new token.
A device reboot is required for Porter to work properly. To continue, please reboot your device.
Another version of this app is installed on your device. To continue, please uninstall all duplicate versions and reboot your device.
The permission of adb is limited

It\'s highly possible that your device manufacturer limits the permission of adb.

There may be a solution for your system in this document.
Run shell commands in terminal apps through Porter
Users have reported that MIUI breaks the Storage Access Framework, which is used by the export function.
If you are using MIUI, you may have to extract the file from the assets folder in Porter\'s APK.
Export the files to a new folder.
Two files will be exported: %1$s and %2$s. If the files already exist in the selected folder, they will be deleted.
Use your terminal app to copy the files to its private files directory.

Tip: If your terminal app\'s home directory (~) is in the private files directory, placing the files there will allow you to run %1$s without writing the path.\n\nOtherwise, you can create an alias for %2$s in your terminal app\'s %3$s configuration file.
Open a shell with the following command:

With %1$s, you can run shell commands in any terminal app.

Tap to learn more about how to use it.

Due to a bug in Android 11-12, wireless debugging does not remember any authorized networks.\n\nYou will need to re-authorize the network on each reboot by tapping \"Allow\" when the authorization dialog pops up.
Automatically restart Porter if it crashes
Porter needs to restart in order to apply this setting.
Battery optimization must be disabled for start on boot/watchdog to work properly.
Please disable battery optimization to use this feature.
Notifications from Porter are blocked, so start on boot and the watchdog cannot tell you when they need attention.
This feature reports what it is doing, and what went wrong, through a notification. Notifications from Porter are currently blocked, so it would run without telling you anything.
Porter is already starting in the background
This service is only supported on TV devices
You can start Porter service now.
Make sure the token in your intent matches the one in Settings under “Control Porter with automation apps”.
Allow the app to use Porter.
Can\'t start service because root permission is not granted or this device is not rooted.
Wireless debugging does not recognize Porter, so Porter could not start in the background. Tap to pair Porter again.
Porter needs WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS to start on boot. Tap to learn how to grant it.
Watchdog restarted the service. Tap to learn about potential fixes to prevent future crashes.

Provides pairing support for devices (e.g., TVs running Android 14+) where notifications or split screen cannot be used.\n\nEnables Porter to extract the pairing code from the wireless debugging pairing screen. It will disable itself once the pairing code is found.

If a code was rejected or the notification disappeared, restart pairing here. Then close Android’s old pairing-code dialog and open a new one. Use the new code; you do not need to clear Porter’s data.
No pairing code was received within one minute. Pairing has stopped. Choose Retry, then open a new pairing-code dialog in Wireless debugging.
The pairing connection timed out. Open a new pairing-code dialog in Wireless debugging and try again.
Pairing failed. Open a new pairing-code dialog in Wireless debugging and try again.
Pairing has stopped because the notification timed out. Choose Retry, then open a new pairing-code dialog in Wireless debugging.
Please leave the pairing-code window open and wait.
Returning to Porter to turn off the pairing accessibility service…
Turning off the pairing accessibility service…
The pairing accessibility service is off. All pairing steps are complete. You can close this window.
The pairing accessibility service is still enabled. Turn it off in Accessibility settings.
Some ADB permissions are restricted by Android.
Stopping Porter disconnects apps that use it. You must start Porter again manually, which may require a computer.
Open service details and stop options
Porter is ready. Compatible apps can now connect and request access.
Porter cannot be started from this Android user or profile. Switch to the device’s primary user, install Porter there if needed, and start its service. Then return here to manage your apps.
Stopping Porter disconnects apps in all Android users. To start it again, switch to the device’s primary user and open Porter there.
Application access is unavailable while the service is stopped or changing.
The previous update did not finish. The service is still running. You can retry the update.
The previous update did not finish. The service is stopped. Go to the dashboard to start it again.
The running service uses a different build from the installed app. Compatible features remain available.
The running service cannot report its build identity. Update it to use the installed build. Compatible features remain available.
You can leave this screen. The operation continues in the background.
Requires a rooted device. Porter requests root access when you press Start.
Updating briefly disconnects connected apps. Existing permissions are kept.
Open Porter in the primary Android user to update the service.
Update the service to enable these features.
After a Porter app update, replace an running service with a different build in the background. This briefly disconnects connected apps. A stopped service stays stopped.
The previous service update did not finish. Retry if the service is still running, or start it again from the Service screen.
Global access control is unavailable in the running service.
The running service does not support the current app discovery and connection history features. Available apps are shown using its older interface.
The running service could not be replaced with the installed version. If it is still running, you can retry. Otherwise, start the service again from the Service screen.
Some profiles could not be checked. This list may be incomplete.
Restart Porter to discover more apps and see connection history.
Apps can connect automatically when Porter starts. The connection time does not indicate when an app was last used.

Pause access for all apps. Their saved permissions are kept.
Restart Porter to use global access control.
Porter is running, but app access is paused. Resume access in Applications.
Porter is based on Shizuku and provides the same access, with its own controls for managing and pausing app access.
Use the compatibility guide for installation options for this build.
Install the compatibility app from the primary Android user.
A Shizuku app is installed for another Android user or profile. Resolve that installation first. Porter will not remove another user’s apps.
Your Shizuku app access choices are saved and ready to import.
Setup did not finish. You can retry.
Restart the Porter service from the home screen to use integrated setup.
Porter will stop %1$s, uninstall it, and install Porter Compatibility in its place. Other Shizuku settings will be deleted.
Shizuku’s app access decisions could not be read. You will need to approve your apps again in Porter.
No additional access choices were found. Existing Porter choices are kept.
Your Shizuku access choices will be carried over automatically. Existing Porter choices are kept.
This device has no screen for allowing app installation. Install the separate compatibility APK using another supported installer or a computer.
Open the installed Shizuku app from Android’s app settings to stop its service.
Your Shizuku apps can use Porter too. Just install the small compatibility app for apps that do not support Porter directly.
The compatibility app helps apps that only recognize Shizuku find and connect to Porter. Install it once and manage access in Porter. Apps with built-in Porter support do not need it.
Start Porter to connect your apps and check usage.
App usage is not available yet.
This includes installed apps that connect through the compatibility app, even if you have not allowed them access yet.
Porter installs the included compatibility app for you.
Start Porter to install the compatibility app automatically.
If compatibility is not working, install the included copy again. Your app access choices in Porter are kept.
The installed version is newer than the copy included with Porter. Keep it, or use its original installer to reinstall that version.
Apps that need this app will lose access until you install it again. Porter keeps your access choices. Porter will remove the app, or open the Android uninstaller if needed.
Android could not open the uninstaller. You can remove Porter Compatibility from Android app settings.
To connect apps that only know Shizuku, Porter needs to replace the installed Shizuku app with its compatibility app. Your app access choices will be carried over.
The service could not be checked. Retrying automatically…
Porter could not stop Shizuku. Stop it in Shizuku, then try again.
Choices are skipped when Porter already has a choice or the app has changed.
Allow access to your local network so Porter can find and connect to Android’s wireless debugging service.
Open Wireless debugging in Android’s developer options and choose Pair device with pairing code. Enter the port and pairing code here.
Porter will run commands on your device for this app, with the same privileges Porter itself has. Only allow apps you trust.
